Why a Savannah house gets two tax bills

Georgia law makes a Savannah owner pay both city and county tax, and the two are mailed separately. The City of Savannah Revenue Department bills the city levy. The Chatham County Tax Commissioner bills county and school board taxes.

  • City Revenue Department: 305 Fahm Street, 912-651-6455, weekdays 8:15 to 5. Mail: P.O. Box 1228, Savannah, GA 31402.
  • Chatham County Board of Assessors, 222 W. Oglethorpe Ave., Suite 113, 912-652-7271, for value, exemptions and appeals.
  • County Tax Commissioner: 912-652-7100.

The city does not value property. City Council picks the millage rate, and the county assessors pick the value it multiplies.

Savannah housing at a glance

Savannah had 147,780 residents in 2020 and an estimated 149,440 in 2025, spread over 58,192 households and 106.85 square miles of land.

Tenants are the majority, with owners in just 45.4 percent of homes. The midpoint owned home is valued at $248,900, midpoint rent is $1,382 and midpoint household income is $57,137. Commuters average 20.7 minutes.

Landlords and investors therefore shape resale demand next to owner-occupants. Rental parcels pay tax without homestead relief, which makes their bills higher for the same value.

City millage rate

The city put forward 11.749 mills for 2026, unchanged from 2025 and billed as the lowest since 1987. Its calculated rollback figure, the rate that would hold revenue flat after reassessment, stood at 11.402.

County, school board and other rates stack on top. Parcels covered by Stephens-Day are shielded from the extra bite that keeping the rate would otherwise pass along as values rise.

When do the installments come due?

The city splits real property into two bills. April brings the first, typically due in mid-June and equal to half of last year's tax. September brings the second, typically due mid-November, repriced for current value, exemptions and rate. Dates are fixed when bills print and can shift.

The county runs real property on a different calendar: first bill mailed by April 1 for June 1, second mailed by September 15 for November 15. Personal property bills fall due by November 15.

Money has to be received and posted on or before the due date, so a mailing delay is your risk. The city takes partial payments through the second due date but arranges no payment plans. An unreceived bill is still owed; copies are online or at the Revenue Department counter.

Late payment costs

State law (O.C.G.A. 48-2-40 to 48-2-44) sets interest at bank prime plus 3 percent a year, added monthly. Four months late, a 5 percent penalty applies to all but small homestead bills, then again after each further four months until it totals 20 percent.

Left alone, an account becomes a fi. fa., a lien that hurts credit and can lead to a tax sale. The city runs roughly six sales a year, advertising each property four weeks before. After a sale the former owner has a year and a day to redeem by repaying the bid plus 20 percent.

While an appeal is open, the city bills at last year's value or 85 percent of the new one, whichever is lower, and collects at the second installment date. A corrected bill or a refund follows the ruling.

Stephens-Day and homestead exemptions

The house has to be your legal residence on January 1, owned and occupied. You can apply at any time of year, though the assessors must have it inside 45 days of the yearly assessment notice for the exemption to start that year. Matching addresses on a Georgia driver's license or ID and a vehicle registration are required, and staff may add a request for a prior utility bill or a voter card.

  • Standard homestead: $12,000 off the county side of assessed value, $2,000 off the school and state sides.
  • Stephens-Day, in place since 1999, and the statewide floating exemption both freeze a base year value. The owner gets whichever saves more.
  • Chatham senior exemption: for owners 65 and older whose net income does not exceed $10,000, it removes $30,000 from the county and school assessed value.

Sales, deed changes and significant improvements move the base. A bedroom addition raises the base by its added value, and a demolition lowers it by the value lost. Opting in or out of HB 581 leaves existing base years alone. Solid waste and street light fees still apply.

Does a short-term rental change my homestead position?

Under the city's vacation rental ordinance, a parcel counts as owner-occupied only if the owner lives in its principal unit as their usual home. Applicants show that with a valid homestead exemption, or with a sworn affidavit plus two items of residency proof.

A homestead claim on a house that is really an investment rental is a problem waiting for a buyer's title review. Check your exemption status with the assessors before listing.

How to appeal a Chatham County value

Put the appeal in writing to the Chatham assessors inside 45 days of the notice, on the state's uniform form, and name your chosen method in that first filing. Valid grounds: taxability, value, uniformity, or an exemption that was denied.

  • Board of Equalization, with Superior Court review available afterward.
  • Arbitration, which needs a certified appraisal delivered inside those same 45 days. The assessors can take it or turn it down, and court review stays open.
  • Hearing officer, reserved for non-homestead real property of $500,000 or more, or certain wireless property over $200,000, on value or uniformity questions.

A surviving spouse or minor child may also petition Probate Court for a year's support, within two years of a death, and an award can relieve tax for the year in the petition.

Where to pay or ask questions

County bills can be paid at tax.chathamcountyga.gov by card or eCheck; the eCheck is free and the card carries a convenience fee. Checks go to P.O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412. Walk-in service is weekdays, 8:30 to 5, at three locations: W. Oglethorpe Ave., Police Memorial Dr. and Eisenhower Dr. Satellite desks on Wilmington Island Rd., US 80 and Georgia Highway 21 see people only by appointment.

County staff also bill for Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Thunderbolt, Tybee Island and Vernonburg. Any returned check is charged 5 percent of its amount, minimum $30. Tangible personal property other than vehicles, trailers and mobile homes is exempt when its total fair market value is $20,000 or less.

Can I sell a Savannah house that owes tax?

Yes. The title company collects payoff figures from the Revenue Department and the Tax Commissioner and settles both out of your proceeds. Any recorded lien turns up in the title search long before the closing date.

  1. Request a city payoff from the Revenue Department at 912-651-6455.
  2. Request a county payoff from the Tax Commissioner at 912-652-7100.
  3. Ask whether a fi. fa. has been filed and what clears it.
  4. See that both amounts appear on the settlement statement.

Cash offers avoid lender appraisals and repair lists. Compare each against a normal listing less repairs, back tax and holding costs.

Frequently asked questions

Which office collects Savannah city property tax?

The city's Revenue Department, at 305 Fahm Street, 912-651-6455. County and school taxes go to a different office, the Chatham County Tax Commissioner.

When does Savannah's second property tax bill come due?

Usually mid-November. County bills are due November 15, and the city fixes its own date when it prints bills.

What is the appeal window in Chatham County?

Forty-five days after the annual notice of assessment, filed first with the Chatham County Board of Assessors.

What happens to a Savannah bill that is 120 days late?

A 5 percent penalty lands, on top of monthly interest at prime plus 3 percent a year, and it repeats each 120 days until it reaches 20 percent.

What does Stephens-Day do for a Chatham County owner?

It is a Chatham-only homestead exemption from 1999 that pins taxable value to a base year figure plus improvements. If the statewide floating exemption saves more, the owner receives that one.

Which county bills you in Atlanta?

Fulton County bills most of the city, but Atlanta also extends into DeKalb County, so check which county your parcel sits in before you call anyone. Atlanta is the county seat of Fulton and spreads across the Fulton and DeKalb line, which means two assessors and two tax commissioners are involved citywide.

For Fulton parcels, the Board of Assessors sets the value and the Fulton County Tax Commissioner bills and collects for Fulton County, Fulton County and City of Atlanta Schools, the State of Georgia, and the City of Atlanta. Fulton has 18 taxing jurisdictions in all, each setting its own rate, and each is listed separately on the bill. For DeKalb parcels, the DeKalb Property Appraisal Department sets values, with the same 40 percent assessment ratio and a 45-day appeal window from the notice date.

  • Fulton Tax Commissioner: 404-613-6100, 141 Pryor Street SW
  • DeKalb Property Appraisal: 404-371-0841

Due dates, interest and penalties

In the 2026 cycle, City of Atlanta taxes were due September 30 and Fulton County taxes and those from all other jurisdictions were due October 15. Expect a similar rhythm in later years, and read the date printed on your bill.

StepTiming

Fulton's 2026 bills were temporary. Final rates are set once the state certifies the digest, and a refund or revised bill goes out only if needed.

Interest begins the day after the due date. An extra 5 percent penalty is added on the 120th day, and another 5 percent every 120 days after that, up to a maximum of 20 percent. The office accepts partial payments, though interest keeps accruing on the unpaid principal.

How to pay an Atlanta property tax bill

Pay online at fultoncountytaxes.org, by phone at 404-613-6100, by mail, or in person at the Tax Commissioner's office in the Fulton County Government Center, 141 Pryor Street SW. The office also operates three other full-service locations.

Mail goes to the Fulton County Tax Commissioner, 141 Pryor St. SW, Suite 1106, Atlanta, GA 30303. The office's website lets you search for a bill by parcel ID, account number or address, and it supports a multi-parcel summary lookup for owners with several properties. Credit card and e-check payments run through the same system. If an expected bill has not arrived by mid-September in a billing year, call rather than wait.

Escrow does not remove the owner's responsibility. If your lender pays the tax, still confirm that the payment posted against the right parcel, particularly after a refinance or a servicer change.

Atlanta housing in brief

Atlanta has an estimated 529,110 residents. Owners are a minority: 46.4 percent of the 236,468 households own. The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $439,600 and the middle monthly rent is $1,711. The city counts 242 officially defined neighborhoods. Three high-rise districts, Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead, run north to south along Peachtree, and most of the land between them is low-density single-family housing with a craftsman bungalow common in older areas. Atlanta annexed Emory into the city effective January 1, 2018.

How to appeal an assessment in Fulton County

File within 45 days of the date on your Notice of Assessment, online at fultonassessor.org, in person at a Board of Assessors office, or by mail. Notices typically go out in June, and the deadline is whatever date is printed on the notice.

The appeal covers the assessed value only, and the estimated tax cannot be appealed. Each appeal must pick one of three paths: a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration on valuation, or a hearing officer, and the last two can carry fees. Hearings are held at 141 Pryor Street, Suite 2111, and the Board of Equalization office takes scheduling calls at 404-613-7792. Useful evidence includes the purchase price, an appraisal, photographs and comparable sales.

Either side can carry a Board of Equalization decision to Superior Court within 30 days of its mailing date. The appeals process can run for months, and a temporary bill issued while an appeal is pending must still be paid or penalties apply. The 2026 notices also carried a new format under Senate Bill 566, with an Estimated Tax Savings section replacing the old estimated tax table.

  • Board of Assessors, Fulton County Center: 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018
  • Customer Service Center: 11575 Maxwell Road
  • North Fulton Customer Service Center: 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210
  • South Fulton Service Center: 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, Suite 224

All four are reached through the same assessor line, 404-612-6440.

Selling while taxes are unpaid

Plan to clear the balance through the closing, since unpaid Atlanta and Fulton tax follows the parcel. Georgia assigns a year's bill to whoever owned the home on January 1, and there is no refund for a partial year if you sell and move.

Ask the Fulton Tax Commissioner for a payoff total that includes interest and any 5 percent penalty steps. The temporary billing used in 2026 adds one wrinkle: because a corrected bill or refund may follow once final rates are set, the closing attorney should agree in the contract how any later adjustment between buyer and seller will be handled.

A buyer's exemption starts fresh. Owners who held the home on January 1 and missed the April 1 homestead deadline can still apply during the appeal period, while owners who bought after January 1 apply for the following tax year.

Steps before you list an Atlanta house

Start by confirming the county. Look up the parcel on the Fulton site, or call DeKalb Property Appraisal at 404-371-0841 if the home sits on that side. Check the balance and the payment status for each jurisdiction, and make sure any lender payment posted to the right parcel.

Next, compare your assessment notice with what you expect to list at. If the value looks high and the appeal window is still open, a filing may help your buyer's first bill too. Last, give the title company a written payoff and a note about the temporary 2026 billing so the contract can say who handles a later refund or revised bill. A cash buyer can move quickly, but these checks still come first.

Frequently asked questions

Were Atlanta property tax bills final in 2026?

No. Fulton County issued temporary bills based on the preliminary 2026 digest and 2025 millage rates, as authorized by the Superior Court. A revised bill or refund follows only after final rates are set.

Is part of Atlanta in DeKalb County?

Yes. Atlanta is the seat of Fulton County and extends into DeKalb County. Parcels in the DeKalb part are valued by DeKalb Property Appraisal rather than the Fulton Board of Assessors, so confirm the county on your bill.

How many days do I have to appeal in Fulton County?

You have 45 days from the date of the Notice of Assessment. After the deadline passes the right to appeal that year's value is lost.

How is a late Atlanta tax bill penalized?

Interest starts the day after the due date. A 5 percent penalty is added on the 120th day and again every 120 days, up to 20 percent total. Fulton accepts partial payments, but interest continues on what remains unpaid.

Which office do I call about my Atlanta home value?

For a Fulton County parcel, call the Board of Assessors at 404-612-6440. For billing or payment questions, call the Fulton Tax Commissioner at 404-613-6100. DeKalb parcels go to DeKalb Property Appraisal at 404-371-0841.

Who bills property tax in Columbus

Because Columbus and Muscogee County merged into one government, a single Tax Commissioner mails every bill and receives every payment in the city. Taxability and value are decided by the Muscogee County Board of Tax Assessors, whose members serve fixed terms under state law and are appointed by City Council.

Council fixes the mill rate for city operations. For the schools, the school board recommends a rate and Council, with few exceptions, must adopt it. Since 2016 Georgia has levied no state ad valorem tax. The Board of Equalization consists of Muscogee County residents named by the grand jury, with the Clerk of Superior Court handling its administration.

  • Tax Commissioner: billing, collection, delinquent accounts, tax sales.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: values, exemptions, appeals. Help desk: 706-225-4398.
  • Board of Equalization: disputes over value, uniformity and exemptions.

The assessors meet Wednesdays at 9:00am at the City Services Building, 3111 Citizens Way.

Selling in Columbus

Columbus is the Muscogee County seat, on the Chattahoochee River opposite Phenix City, Alabama, roughly 100 miles southwest of Atlanta. Only one Georgia city is bigger.

Population was estimated at 202,171 in 2025, a 2.3% drop since 2020. Just 50.8% of homes are owner-occupied. The typical owned home is valued at $193,900, and rent averages $1,106. With so many rentals, plenty of Columbus sellers are landlords, and a rental's tax bill follows the January 1 owner like any other.

Property tax calendar

The Tax Commissioner lays out the year month by month: notices of assessment in May, bills in August, first payment in October.

Columbus property tax dates by month
MonthWhat happens
April 1Mobile home bills due; homestead deadline; business personal property, aircraft and watercraft returns due
MayAnnual notice of assessment mailed; appeals within 45 days of the notice date
JulyTaxing authorities advertise and set millage rates
AugustReal and personal property bills mailed
OctoberBills due: a 40% installment or payment in full
DecemberRemaining 60% due

During the appeal window you can file a homestead application instead of an appeal. Exact payment days are on your bill.

Installments and closing

Owners may pay 40% in October and the other 60% in December, or settle everything in October. A sale that closes between the two payments should come with a note to the title company about what is already paid.

Legal responsibility for a year's tax rests with the January 1 owner, whoever holds the house afterward. Buyer and seller can both receive a bill. The office leaves the question of who pays what share to the closing documents.

If the tax is never paid, the lien lands on whoever owned on January 1 unless the seller proves, within 90 days of the due date, that the buyer assumed it. Proof can be a recorded deed naming the new owner, or closing language that plainly hands the tax to the buyer. Once checked, the lien can be recorded against the buyer instead.

Homestead exemptions

The standard exemption cuts assessed value by $13,500. The Tax Commissioner also lists exemptions for age, military service and surviving spouses. File any time after the property becomes your primary residence, with April 1 as the last day for the year you want it.

  • Standard homestead (H1): $13,500 off assessed value for county and school board maintenance and operation levies, but not bond debt.
  • Elderly general (H2): 65 or older by January 1, household net income no higher than $10,000 the year before, with income documents.
  • Disabled veteran (H5): up to $121,812, with a VA benefits letter.
  • Unremarried surviving spouse of a service member killed in war or armed conflict: up to $121,812, backed by Department of Defense papers.
  • Surviving spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed or fatally hurt on duty: full 100% exemption.

Bring the recorded deed and a Georgia driver's license showing your current address. Voter and vehicle registration must both be in Muscogee County. Once approved, the exemption renews until you move, ownership changes or you switch to a different one. A property tax deferral exists for owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less, running until a change of ownership or until the deferred tax and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

Checklist before you list

Start with what you owe today. Request a payoff figure from the Tax Commissioner and pass it to the title company so the closing statement carries the right amount. When the closing falls between the October and December payments, note which installment has been paid.

  • Locate your latest notice of assessment and file it with the deed.
  • Check whether the house carries a homestead exemption. The buyer will need their own.
  • Should the buyer take on the year's tax, have the closing documents say so plainly and obtain a recorded deed in the buyer's name, so the 90-day proof is on hand.
  • For a rental, tell the tenants about the sale and put the lease in the closing file.

A cash buyer can often close faster than one relying on a lender. The tax steps are identical.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Unpaid taxes, liens and tax sales

For delinquent accounts the Tax Commissioner can file a lien known as a fifa and levy the property toward a tax sale. Liens and lien certificates are never sold by the office. A parcel that draws no buyer at a sale is offered again later. The Delinquent Tax section carries the sale list and a registration page for a bidder class.

Staff are not allowed to give legal advice, so an owner facing a lien or levy should talk to an attorney. For a seller, the practical sequence is simple: get the payoff from the Tax Commissioner, confirm it with the title company, and clear the lien from the sale proceeds if the house sells before a tax sale date. A cash sale suits this well, because the payoff and title work are the only steps between you and the closing table.

Personal property has its own rule. Taxable tangible personal property other than motor vehicles, trailers and mobile homes is exempt when its total fair market value, as determined by the assessors, does not exceed $20,000.

How to challenge your value

Appeals are due 45 days after the date on the notice of assessment, which goes out in May. The Board of Tax Assessors receives and reviews the appeal, and the Board of Equalization hears matters of value, uniformity, taxability and denied exemptions.

Real property appeals go to ccgboa@columbusga.org, and personal property appeals go to ppboa@columbusga.org. Questions about real property appeals can also go to 706-225-4398. A homeowner who has not yet claimed a homestead can file that application during the same appeal period instead of appealing.

Keep the notice itself. It states the value the county will use for the bill, and the 45 days run from the date printed on it.

Frequently asked questions

When are Columbus property tax bills due?

In October, as either a 40% installment or payment in full, with the remaining 60% due in December. The exact day is printed on your bill.

Who is responsible for Columbus property tax after I sell?

The person who owned the property on January 1 is legally responsible for that year's tax. Closing documents normally divide it, and a lien moves to the buyer only with proof delivered within 90 days of the due date.

How much is the standard homestead exemption in Columbus?

It is a $13,500 reduction in assessed value. It applies to the county and school maintenance and operation levies, not the bond portion.

What is the appeal deadline in Columbus?

45 days from the date of the assessment notice, which is mailed in May. A homestead application can be filed in place of an appeal during that window.

Does the Columbus Tax Commissioner sell tax liens?

No. The office does not sell its tax liens or lien certificates. A property that does not sell at a tax sale returns to the rotation for future sales.

Partial payments are accepted once bills are mailed, and penalties and interest continue on whatever remains.

A balance left unpaid can become a lien. The office first mails a 30-day notice of intent, then issues the lien, called a Fi.Fa. It is entered on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court, lasts seven years, and can appear on credit reports. Paying everything owed, including fees, penalties and interest, cancels it.

Millage rates by tax district

Georgia's third-largest city, with about 201,999 residents, sits across the Savannah River from North Augusta, South Carolina, and spreads over more than 300 square miles.

Home prices run well under Atlanta's. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $178,400. Fort Gordon, Augusta University and the Savannah River Site are the largest employers, which means military and medical moves drive a lot of the buying and selling.

Appeals and homestead applications

You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice to appeal, and the same window works for a homestead application if you missed the earlier filing date. Notices usually mail in late June.

Do not mistake the notice for a bill. It lists assessed value, exemptions and your appeal rights, and since Senate Bill 566 it carries an Estimated Tax Savings section where the old estimated tax tables used to be. File online with the Property Search tool at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com, or send it by mail or email, or bring it in. Augusta also has a local floating homestead exemption that limits certain increases in assessed value on qualifying primary residences.

Homestead applications go to the Tax Commissioner, which forwards them to the Board of Assessors for the final decision. A denial can be appealed to the Board of Equalization. An exemption renews automatically, and you do not have to apply again unless the ownership, name or deed changes. Refinancing does not affect it, and all vehicles owned by the applicant and spouse must be registered in Richmond County. When mailing an application, use certified mail, because metered postage dates are not accepted as timely.

What happens to the tax when you sell

Whoever owned the house on January 1 is billed for the year, though the purchase agreement can shift that cost to the buyer at closing. Your closing attorney sorts out the split.

A sale in, say, July still sends the bill to the earlier owner. Behind on payments? The office refreshes balances every night, so ask for the current figure and put the bill number or map and parcel number on any written request. A property can also show as under appeal or pending an assessment change order, in which case the bill may not yet be due, so confirm the status before paying.

If delinquent taxes lead to a tax sale, the county auctions the parcel on a first Tuesday in the Commission Chambers at 535 Telfair Street, after running a notice in the Augusta Chronicle for four straight weeks. Selling first lets the closing pay the county out of your proceeds.

Look up your parcel at augustarichmondtaxassessor.com and write down the tax district, because that district fixes the rate your buyer will pay. Then phone 706-821-2391 for the balance and make sure the Clerk of Superior Court shows no Fi.Fa. against the parcel. Tell buyers that a homestead exemption is theirs to file for.

Give the closing attorney the balance, the bill number and any open appeal status so the settlement statement is right, and keep copies of each written answer from the county in case a question comes up after closing. What is the due date for Augusta property tax?

November 30. Owners who pay within the first 20 days get a 1 percent discount on the tax portion. After the due date, monthly interest applies and a one-time 10 percent penalty follows in late December.

Is Augusta's property tax rate the same everywhere in Richmond County?

No. The county lists four tax districts for 2026: Urban at 28.284, County with fire at 26.28, Hephzibah at 24.939 and Blythe with fire at 26.839. The district printed on your bill decides the rate.

How long do I have to appeal an Augusta assessment?

You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. Once that window closes, the right to appeal that year's value ends, and the next chance comes with the following year's notice.

What does FLOST do for Augusta homeowners?

FLOST is a 0.5 percent sales tax that began October 1, 2026, with proceeds used to cut property taxes. Rollbacks appear on tax bills starting in 2027, as a reduction to a portion of the county's general operating levy.

Who do I call about an Augusta property value?

Call the Richmond County Board of Assessors at 706-821-2310. For billing, payments or homestead questions, call the Tax Commissioner's office at 706-821-2391.

The taxed share is 40 percent.

An owner has 45 days to appeal. The city's calendar uses the end of that window as a second deadline for homestead applications. While an appeal is open, Cobb Tax prints two amounts on the bill: the regular tax and a lower appeal amount based on 85 percent of assessed value or 100 percent of the prior value nobody contested. Late payment costs

An owner who never receives a bill still owes the tax, so print the bill from Cobb's website if yours goes missing.

Escrow can complicate things. When a mortgage servicer asks for the bill, Cobb sends one to both servicer and owner, and refunds a duplicate payment. The city copies the original to the servicer and a copy to the owner when notified in time. Verify which bill your escrow account actually paid.

Clearing taxes before a sale

In Marietta, taxes follow the property, so the current owner answers for anything outstanding.

  2. Ask both for written payoff figures and whether a lien has been filed.
  3. Hand the figures to the closing attorney.

Cobb County bills are due October 15. City of Marietta bills mail from late August and fall due at the end of October. Check the date printed on each bill.

Which office bills the City of Marietta tax?

The City of Marietta Tax Division, at 205 Lawrence Street, 770-794-5680. Its bill covers the city, Marietta City Schools, Gateway Marietta CID and the downtown authority.

Who hears a Marietta value appeal?

The Cobb County Board of Tax Assessors receives it, inside 45 days of the notice. The city does not set value and sends valuation questions to the Cobb assessors.

Yes. The city allows 85 percent of the billed amount by the due date, and Cobb prints a lower appeal amount to be paid by October 15. Interest can apply if the final value arrives later.

The tax follows the property, and the current owner is responsible for what is outstanding. Bills go to the January 1 owner, so the sale contract should say who reimburses whom.

Public safety splits by territory. Who bills and who values

The Macon-Bibb County Tax Commissioner sends the bill, and the money is split among the State of Georgia, Macon-Bibb County and the Board of Education. The county commissioners and the school board vote the millage rates. Values are the Tax Assessors' job. The commissioner is an independent elected office, separate from the assessors and from the county commissioners, so send value questions to one and payment questions to the other.

  • Tax Commissioner: phone 478-621-6500, email taxinfo@maconbibb.us, website maconbibbtax.us. The office bills, collects, distributes the money and prepares the digest for the state each year.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: 688 Walnut Street, Suite 200, Macon, GA 31201, phone (478) 200-5550, website bibbassessors.com.
  • Deed room at the Macon-Bibb County Courthouse, 601 Mulberry St., for copies of a warranty deed.

Macon-Bibb housing snapshot

Macon-Bibb County is the largest of its neighbors, with an estimated 157,556 residents in mid-2025, almost level with the 157,358 counted for 2020. It covers 249.38 square miles and has 59,921 households. Owners live in 51.4% of homes, so rentals are common. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $174,500, and median gross rent runs $1,066.

The garbage fee on your tax bill

Every residential premises meant for occupancy, vacant or not, is billed for garbage service, and the Solid Waste Department's service is mandatory. Garbage is billed quarterly, with due dates at the end of each quarter.

  • Appealing a property value does not pause the garbage fee, which stays due in full.
  • Low-income owners may seek an exemption by applying at the Solid Waste Department, 327 Lower Poplar St., before the 5:00 p.m. cutoff on November 1 of each year.
  • If a home is destroyed by fire or casualty or demolished, the owner must notify the Solid Waste Director in writing right away.

Solid Waste handles service questions at 478.803.0499 or garbage@maconbibb.us. When you request a payoff, ask the commissioner whether a garbage charge is still open.

Returns, homestead and appeals

To get a value review, you must file a return by April 1. Skipping it blocks any review. Returns go to the Tax Assessors' Office, which mails a notice when it disagrees with your figure.

You then have 45 days from the notice date. The written appeal goes to the Board of Assessors and has to name the method you choose. Call the assessors before you file if you are unsure how to proceed.

The Tax Assessors' Office approves homestead applications. Eligibility turns on January 1, when you must be both owner and resident. An application in hand before April 1 counts for that year, and a move or a deed change calls for a fresh one. Mobile home owners who dispute the assessed value get the later of two deadlines: 45 days after the bill is mailed, or April 1.

What happens if you do not pay

State law attaches interest and penalties to any tax left unpaid beyond the due date. Before the office issues a lien (FiFa), it mails a notice of intent giving 30 days to pay in full. Mobile homes paid late face a state-mandated penalty of 10 percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, plus monthly interest.

  • Sales happen at 11 AM on the courthouse steps at the United Building in Central City Park, 206 7th Street, on the first Tuesday of any month with a sale on the calendar.
  • The winning bidder buys a Sheriff's Tax Deed, pays within two hours, and can use cash, certified funds or money orders only.
  • The owner can redeem for 12 months, at a price that can include the bid, later taxes the buyer paid, special assessments and a 20% premium.
  • The buyer cannot cut off that right until a year after the sale.

Money from a sale beyond the taxes and costs is called excess funds, and the commissioner holds it. A mortgage company or lienholder may claim it before the owner, and competing claims can end up in Superior Court.

After a Macon-Bibb tax sale

When a sale is scheduled, the list runs in The Telegraph's legal advertisements every Tuesday for four weeks beforehand. To ask about a delinquent property that is not on a list, call the Levy Department at 478-621-6500. The opening bid is the tax due plus penalties and fees, and extra costs for title research and advertising are added once a property is picked for sale.

The winning bidder holds a Sheriff's Tax Deed rather than a clean title, and Georgia law bars the buyer from taking possession, making improvements or evicting tenants right away. To cut off the owner's right to redeem once the 12 months pass, the buyer has to send certified mail to the record owner and every interest holder, then run a newspaper notice weekly for four straight weeks. A quiet title petition comes next, and the court appoints a Special Master to decide who was owed notice.

Macon-Bibb County does not assist with redemption or its foreclosure, so an owner facing a sale should get professional advice quickly.

Selling a Macon house with tax due

Whoever is on record as owner at the start of the year gets the bill. When a transfer is reported to the office within the 90 days leading up to the due date, the new owner is billed instead. Ownership data comes from deeds recorded at the courthouse and relayed by the assessors.

  1. If you close between billing and the due dates, ask the commissioner at 478-621-6500 for a payoff that covers both installments.
  2. Give the closing attorney that figure along with any open garbage charge.
  3. Confirm a lien has not been filed.

Lenders with escrow accounts get a data file, yet paying the tax remains the owner's job. Boats, aircraft and business equipment work the same way: whoever owned the item at New Year's owes the full year, even after a sale or a relocation, and the assessors want proof before they remove the account. A cash buyer will still want the account clear at closing.

Frequently asked questions

Which installment dates apply to Macon property tax?

October 15 and November 15, after statements are mailed by September 15. A weekend date moves forward.

Which number reaches the Macon tax office?

The Macon-Bibb County Tax Commissioner answers at 478-621-6500. For value questions, call the Board of Tax Assessors at (478) 200-5550.

Does Macon accept postmarks on mailed property tax payments?

Yes, but only a dated postal-service postmark counts toward the current year's tax, not a meter stamp.

When is the Macon homestead exemption deadline?

The office needs it before April 1 for it to count that year, and you have to own and occupy the home on January 1.

When are Macon-Bibb tax sales held?

At 11 AM on the first Tuesday of a month with a sale scheduled, on the steps at the United Building in Central City Park. A bidder or representative has to be present.
